subject: The Top Takes from Newcomer’s Cerebral Valley AI Summit
notes: Recap of speaker sessions at the Cerebral Valley AI Summit held the previous week. Email is truncated ("too long for email"); slides and survey results not in the visible text. Funding figures are cited in passing as context, not reported as new deals. Crosby's $85 million may be a cumulative total; the issue does not say. Fireworks' $17.5 billion July valuation is recorded as a fact on the security-incident story because the issue names no round.

stories.headline: River AI has raised $1 billion in a seed round from General Catalyst, AMP PBC, Nvidia and AMD
stories.quote: River AI has raised $1 billion from General Catalyst and AMP PBC, as well as Nvidia and AMD. Babuschkin joked that the 10-figure seed round was “table stakes” for AI these days.
stories.description: Software to post-train and serve models on companies' own hardware

stories.headline: Crosby has raised $85 million from investors including Lux Capital, Index Ventures and Sequoia
stories.quote: Crosby has raised $85 million from investors such as Lux Capital, Index Ventures, and Sequoia.
stories.description: Law firm entity selling legal AI to non-lawyers

stories.headline: Summit attendees optimistic about Anthropic's upcoming IPO; survey expects $1-2 trillion market cap after first day
stories.quote: there was also near-unanimous optimism about the upcoming IPO of Anthropic.

facts.text: Summit audience survey expected Anthropic's market cap after the first day of trading to be between $1 and $2 trillion
facts.quote: Yet the room also thought that Anthropic’s market cap after the first day of trading would sit between $1 and $2 trillion.

stories.headline: Databricks CEO says 2026 is a bad year to go public but Databricks will list eventually
stories.quote: Ghodsi also stood by his call that 2026 is a bad year to go public, but he doesn’t believe in staying private forever and Databricks will list eventually.

stories.headline: Perplexity CEO says the company could IPO any time between now and 2028
stories.quote: Srinivas did not comment on the company’s numbers or financials but said it is “doing pretty well enough that we could IPO any time from now to 2028.”
stories.description: AI company now primarily serving enterprise customers

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia discussed by summit speakers as a risk to AI ecosystem continuity
stories.quote: As for Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia, it leaves a “huge concern” about continuity in AI industry leadership, Taneja said.

facts.text: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi said Huang had served as a financial backstop and his exit will start hurting players on the margin
facts.quote: “Whenever there was hesitation and things on the bubble, he was there to say, don’t worry about it, I got their back,” Ghodsi said. “That’s no longer there. So I think on the margin, it’s going to start hurting a lot of players.”

facts.text: Nikesh Arora, floated as a potential Nvidia CEO, deflected and said the departure would likely cause short-term instability
facts.quote: Although Shaun Maguire and other tech leaders were floating his name as a potential Nvidia CEO, Arora deflected on the question. He said Huang’s departure would likely lead to short-term instability but would hardly be a death knell for the firm.

facts.text: Igor Babuschkin said Huang's resignation creates uncertainty for open-weight model advocates
facts.quote: Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia creates “a lot of uncertainty” for open-weight advocates, Babuschkin said, calling Huang the “leader of the pack” when it came to open-weight models.

stories.headline: Fireworks disclosed a major security incident last week, described by its CEO as "LLM jacking"
stories.quote: also addressed a major security incident that Fireworks, an inference provider, disclosed last week. She described it as “LLM jacking”: an organized attack, possibly by people with a crypto-jacking background, aimed at monetizing compute and tokens.

facts.text: Fireworks was valued at $17.5 billion in July
facts.quote: Qiao, whose company was valued at $17.5 billion in July, also addressed a major security incident that Fireworks, an inference provider, disclosed last week.

facts.text: Fireworks worked with Palo Alto Networks on forensics and used CrowdStrike and Wiz sensors for detection
facts.quote: Fireworks worked with Palo Alto Networks on forensics and used CrowdStrike and Wiz sensors for detection, she said

stories.headline: Market swoon on Monday followed summit survey in which 79% saw an AI bubble
stories.quote: In our audience survey, 79% of respondents agreed that there was an AI bubble and 67% of them thought it was likely to pop in 2027 — and that was before Monday’s market swoon.

facts.text: 64% of survey respondents were hiring fewer people; none said they were hiring significantly more because of AI
facts.quote: Another stat of note: 64% of respondents were also hiring fewer people, and not a single person said that they were hiring significantly more because of AI.

stories.headline: Bessemer and Newcomer's inaugural AI 100 list totals $3.6 trillion in valuation, 55% from OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.quote: The total valuation for the inaugural Cloud 100 list in 2016 was $100 billion; for the inaugural AI 100, it’s 36 times higher, at $3.6 trillion.

facts.text: OpenAI and Anthropic account for 55% of the AI 100 valuation total; 20% of listed companies did not exist two years ago
facts.quote: A lot of this value is concentrated in the big foundation model labs, especially OpenAI and Anthropic, which accounted for 55% of the valuation total. Startups on the list are also younger than their predecessors: 20% of the companies on the AI 100 didn’t exist two years ago.

facts.text: About $8 trillion of AI capex is planned over five years, needing close to $6 trillion of annual revenue to justify it, per Bessemer
facts.quote: About $8 trillion of capex for the AI buildout is planned for the next five years, but for that to pay off, businesses would need close to $6 trillion of annual revenue to justify those expenses, per Bessemer’s data.
